# Default settings for the upload service. device-logs.aws.region and device-logs.storage.bucket
# have no default here. Each environment sets them in cloud8-config-service-backend, and the app
# does not start without them.
#
# Still to add:
# - server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout: 130 s (longer than the ALB idle timeout of 120 s).
# - server.shutdown: graceful.
# - device-logs.* defaults: rate limit 30 per 10 min, in-flight cap 200.
server:
  port: 1296
  # Stops Tomcat's RemoteIpValve, which Spring Boot adds on Kubernetes, from moving the ALB's
  # X-Forwarded-For entry into getRemoteAddr() before AlbHeaderTrust reads it (ADR 0004).
  # Don't override this or cloud8.config.forwarded-headers in cloud8-config-service-backend.
  forward-headers-strategy: none
spring:
  mvc:
    formcontent:
      filter:
        # Stops FormContentFilter reading a PUT body sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded before
        # the checks run, which would also make Tomcat send 100 Continue (ADR 0009).
        enabled: false
  servlet:
    multipart:
      # Stops DispatcherServlet parsing a multipart/* body before it picks the handler, for the same
      # reason. Phones never send multipart.
      enabled: false
management:
  server:
    port: 1297
device-logs:
  # The names AWS gives the headers the ALB adds after the mTLS handshake.
  trust:
    subject: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Subject
    issuer: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Issuer
    validity: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Validity
    serial-number: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number
    leaf: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Leaf
    forwarded-for: X-Forwarded-For
  # One entry per contract FileType, or the app does not start. A disabled type gets 403, and a
  # Content-Length above max-size gets 413.
  file-types:
    app-log:
      enabled: true
      max-size: 10MB
    boot-log:
      enabled: true
      max-size: 10MB
    # Personal data. Stays off until the privacy review says yes (ADR 0008).
    calls-xml:
      enabled: false
      max-size: 10MB
  storage:
    # Below the ALB idle timeout of 120 s, so the phone hears 429 from the service instead of a
    # timeout from the ALB. Change it together with the ALB and Tomcat values (ADR 0005).
    write-timeout: 60s
cloud8:
  config:
    # Stops cloud8's ForwardedHeaderFilter from removing X-Forwarded-For before AlbHeaderTrust
    # reads it (ADR 0004).
    forwarded-headers:
      enabled: false
  security:
    # Replaces cloud8's /public/** default, so it is listed again. cloud8 turns CSRF off for
    # every public path, and phones carry no JWT.
    public-paths:
      - /public/**
      - /logs/**

# Architecture decision records (ADRs)

One file per decision, numbered in order (`0001-short-title.md`). Start each new record from `0000-template.md`.

Each record will hold:

- **Status:** Proposed, Accepted, or Superseded by a later record. A changed decision gets a new record; the old one is never rewritten.
- **Context:** the problem and the facts that shaped it.
- **Options:** the choices we looked at, with what each one means.
- **Decision:** what we picked and why.
- **Consequences:** what this makes easier or harder, and what would make us revisit it.
- **Rules for agents:** the one-line hard rule the decision implies, so a proposed change can be checked against it.

## Accepted (stubs, to be written in full)

0001 to 0009: the ALB through the cloud8-common-chart ingress, the DigiCert server certificate, the TLS policy, defensive header parsing, timeouts, public paths, accepted file types, calls.xml, and status codes.

0010 to 0015: the per-pod rate limit, the S3 key with a create-only write, EKS Pod Identity for the upload service, AWS SDK v2, Java 17, and the herd-endpoints namespace.

0016: GitHub issues and a two-branch flow (develop and master), replacing the design doc's GitFlow branches and HERD-NNNN names.

0017 to 0024: the processor and its DynamoDB index. S3 events straight to SQS, one HeadObject per object, the customer from herd-device-api, unknown MACs as "unassigned", create-only rows, the customer index, the configuration defaults, and keys that do not parse failing through redrive (which differs from the design doc). Production configuration values are set per environment later.

## Decided in the design doc, no record yet

- Repo and workflow decisions (p.45 to p.58): repo name, required check (the build8 job), one ruleset for master and develop, auto-deploy develop to stage, build8 tags as the only release versions. CODEOWNERS stays empty until it is needed.

## Open decisions (no record yet)

None right now. When a "Decided: ?" in the design doc becomes relevant, code that depends on it must not pick an option on its own; ask, then add the record.

content.text:
Raising the S3 deadline to 150 s on its own breaks an accepted ADR. ADR 0005 fixes the order **S3 write 60 s < ALB idle 120 s < Tomcat keep-alive 130 s**, and its rule is "Change these three values together, keeping the order." A 150 s write is longer than both the ALB and Tomcat values. Under CLAUDE.md, a change that contradicts an ADR means stop and ask. The ADR README also says a changed decision gets a new ADR that supersedes 0005, rather than an edit to 0005. So this needs a person's decision and a new ADR before any code changes.

**What has to change and where each value is set**

| Value | Now | Must become | Where it's set |
|---|---|---|---|
| S3 write deadline | 60 s | 150 s | `upload-service/src/main/resources/application.yml:55` (`device-logs.storage.write-timeout`). It becomes `apiCallTimeout` in `storage/s3/S3ClientConfig.java:30`. Environments may override it in cloud8-config-service-backend, which isn't in the repo. |
| ALB idle timeout | 120 s | more than 150 s | So far only planned in the comment at `upload-service/src/main/helm/device-log-upload-service-chart/values.yaml:7`. It is a Helm/ingress value, and you'd need to say whether it's a repo default or set per environment in GDS. |
| Tomcat keep-alive | 130 s | more than the new ALB value | Not set yet: it's listed under "Still to add" in `application.yml:6` (`server.tomcat.keep-alive-timeout`). |
| Pod termination grace period | 150 s | probably more than the write deadline (my inference, not stated in the repo) | Comment at `values.yaml:4`. Graceful shutdown is also still to add (`application.yml:7`). As it stands, a 150 s write wouldn't fit inside a 150 s grace period. |
| Envoy (local ALB stand-in) | 120 s | the same as the new ALB value | `local/envoy/envoy.yaml:47` and `:49` (`stream_idle_timeout`, `idle_timeout`), and `:115` (upstream `idle_timeout`). Keep the route's `timeout: 0s` at `:72`. |

**Tests and docs that mention 60 s or 120 s**
- `DeviceLogsPropertiesTest.java:86-91` checks the `application.yml` default of 60 s, so it will fail until it's updated. Other tests that build `Storage(..., 60s)` themselves don't depend on the default.
- `openapi.yaml:119` ("60 s deadline"), `DeviceLogsProperties.java:71-72` (Javadoc), the `application.yml:53-54` comment, `upload-service/ARCHITECTURE.md:7`, `local/CLAUDE.md:59`, `envoy.yaml:46,70,110`.
- Nothing checks the order at startup: `Storage` only has `@DurationMin(seconds = 1)` (`DeviceLogsProperties.java:74`). A 150 s value starts without complaint, so the mistake would only show up in production.

**What goes wrong if only the S3 value changes**
- The ALB gives up first. A write that runs past 120 s gets the ALB's own timeout instead of the service's 429 (STORAGE_FAILED), which is exactly what ADR 0005 and the `application.yml` comment are meant to prevent.
- S3 may still commit the object after the client has gone (`LogStorage.java:18-19`, `openapi.yaml:119-120`). The phone sees a failure for a file that may actually be stored, and may upload it again.
- The order is reversed against Tomcat too (150 s > 130 s), and in-flight writes can be cut off at shutdown by the 150 s grace period.
- Local Envoy keeps cutting at 120 s, so local runs show the same problem.

The processor's 60 s SQS visibility timeout isn't affected. It only starts once S3 has committed the object.

**Files used**
- `CLAUDE.md`, `upload-service/CLAUDE.md`, `local/CLAUDE.md`
- `docs/architecture/decisions/0005-timeout-order.md`, `docs/architecture/decisions/README.md`
- `upload-service/src/main/resources/application.yml`
- `upload-service/src/main/helm/device-log-upload-service-chart/values.yaml`
- `upload-service/src/main/java/.../config/DeviceLogsProperties.java`, `.../storage/s3/S3ClientConfig.java`, `.../storage/LogStorage.java`
- `upload-service/openapi.yaml`, `upload-service/ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `upload-service/src/test/java/.../config/DeviceLogsPropertiesTest.java`
- `local/envoy/envoy.yaml`
